meta.title: CNY → USD channels

status_legend.lawful: Expressly permitted by an official rule, subject only to documented procedure.
status_legend.conditional: Permitted only if the facts fit (specific source of funds, specific applicant status, or specific approval).
status_legend.prohibited: Expressly banned; administrative fine and/or confiscation.

meta.cap_rule: Where a limit could not be confirmed from an official source it is left blank and marked 'unverified'.

channels.name: Emigrant property transfer
channels.name_zh: 移民财产转移
channels.applies_to: A natural person who has emigrated from mainland China to a foreign country (or HK/Macau) and now holds foreign permanent residence or foreign citizenship
channels.best_for: A large balance that represents lawful property you owned before you emigrated
channels.cap: No statutory ceiling. Applications up to RMB 500,000 are decided by the local SAFE branch; anything above goes to SAFE headquarters after local review.
channels.requirements: One single application for the whole amount; written application; applicant information form; business application form; passport plus 中国户籍注销证明 (cancelled PRC household registration) plus embassy-issued or authenticated proof of settlement abroad; proof of the property rights; tax certificate or tax-payment certificate from the competent tax authority; application filed with SAFE where your pre-emigration household registration was located.
pros: The only personal channel in the rulebook with no fixed amount ceiling — designed for exactly this problem.
Explicitly permits the bank to buy FX and remit abroad (售汇＋汇出) at the approved amount.
Staged remittance is built in: up to 50% first, up to half the remainder after one year, the balance after two years; totals of RMB 200,000 or less can be remitted in one go.
Funds are wired straight to your own overseas account, so the money lands in your name with a clean paper trail for US purposes.
cons: You must be able to produce a cancelled-household-registration certificate — if you never held 户口, or the record cannot be located, this route can fail at the first document.
Only property you owned before you obtained emigration status qualifies; assets acquired afterwards do not.
You cannot apply in instalments — one application for the whole amount, even though the payout is staged.
Approval is discretionary; the FX authority refuses applications over property that is legally restricted, subject to litigation, or whose lawful source cannot be shown.
Requires a PRC tax clearance first — and cancelling 户口 itself triggers a pre-cancellation tax settlement under the IIT Law.
Slow: the staged payout alone spans two years.
channels.timeline: Approval: no published service standard (unverified). Payout: 50% / +1 yr / +2 yrs unless the total is ≤ RMB 200,000.
channels.verdict: Primary route for a large balance
channels.note: Art. 6 and Art. 8–11 of the 2004 Measures; SAFE's own Q&A confirms that only someone who already holds foreign permanent residence or citizenship may apply.

channels.name: Inheritance transfer
channels.name_zh: 继承财产转移
channels.applies_to: A foreign citizen (or HK/Macau/Taiwan resident) who has lawfully inherited assets in mainland China
channels.best_for: Money that came to you as an inheritance, not as your own savings
channels.cap: No statutory ceiling; same RMB 500,000 local / above-that headquarters split as emigrant transfer.
channels.requirements: Single application for the whole inherited estate; notarised proof of inheritance; proof of the deceased's property rights; tax certificate or tax-payment certificate from where the estate was located; passport plus embassy-issued or authenticated proof of settlement abroad; application filed with SAFE where the deceased's household registration was located.
pros: Separate, purpose-built channel; not limited by the annual facilitation quota.
Inheritance from different deceased persons is applied for separately, so each estate can be handled on its own.
Remittance may be made in one or several tranches once approved.
cons: Only works if the funds genuinely are inherited property — your own savings cannot be dressed up as an inheritance.
Notarisation of the inheritance and of the property documents is normally required.
Tax clearance on the estate must be obtained first.
Cash withdrawal is prohibited; funds must go to your own overseas account.
channels.verdict: Viable only if the money is inherited
channels.note: Art. 2, Art. 9–11 of the 2004 Measures; SAFE Q&A Q3, Q8, Q11.

channels.name: Non-resident converting lawful current-account RMB income
channels.name_zh: 境外个人经常项目合法人民币收入购汇
channels.applies_to: 境外个人 — a foreign passport holder. This is the category a US citizen falls into under the individual FX rules.
channels.best_for: Salary, service fees, rent or similar income you earned inside China and still hold in RMB
channels.cap: No annual quota is imposed on this route — the rules make the annual USD 50,000 total apply to 结汇 and to 境内个人购汇 only. The bank instead checks that the income and the amount are genuine.
channels.requirements: Valid ID plus documents showing the transaction amount and its source — for income items the rules expressly require tax documents (含税务凭证). The individual FX rules require the bank to verify authenticity and to stop splitting designed to evade limits.
pros: Not capped by the USD 50,000 annual total, because that total is framed for residents' purchases and for everyone's sales of FX.
Can be repeated per income event, so it is not a one-shot application.
Once the money is in your FX savings account, remitting it abroad needs only your ID.
Comes with a natural paper trail (contract, payslips, tax receipts) that also supports your US filing.
cons: Restricted to current-account income — it does not cover capital gains, property sale proceeds or investment returns.
The bank, not you, decides whether the documentation is sufficient; refusals are not appealable in a simple process.
Requires Chinese tax documents, so any untaxed income must be regularised first.
This is the category most often misread: it does not apply if the bank has you on file as a 境内个人.
channels.timeline: Same-day to a few days per transaction, subject to bank review (unverified).
channels.verdict: Best route if the money is China-earned income
channels.note: Art. 13 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3; Art. 13(1) and Art. 2 of 汇发[2007]1号; Art. 37 of the Measures defines who is 境外个人.

channels.name: Re-conversion of unused RMB against the original exchange memo
channels.name_zh: 原兑换未用完的人民币兑回
channels.best_for: RMB that came from foreign currency you personally exchanged into CNY in the first place
channels.cap: Limited to the amount of the original exchange; the original exchange memo is valid for 24 months from the exchange date. Same-day exchanges of up to USD 500 equivalent (and up to USD 1,000 at border points before departure) need only ID.
channels.requirements: Valid ID plus the original exchange memo (原兑换水单) for amounts above the small-value thresholds.
pros: Mechanically simple: the memo proves the RMB is just your own returned foreign currency, so no new quota is used.
Expressly written into the implementing rules, so front-line bank staff should recognise it.
Converts a stale RMB balance back into the currency it came from.
cons: Hard 24-month window from the date of the original exchange — older balances are outside the rule.
Only covers what actually came in as FX; RMB earned inside China does not qualify.
You need the physical or electronic memo; if it is lost this route is closed.
channels.verdict: Fast win if you kept the exchange memos
channels.note: Art. 15 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3; Art. 13(2) of 汇发[2007]1号.

channels.name: Remitting FX already sitting in a foreign-currency savings account
channels.name_zh: 境外个人外汇储蓄账户汇出境外
channels.best_for: A balance that is already in USD or another foreign currency rather than RMB
channels.cap: No amount limit stated for account transfers; cash carried out over USD 10,000 needs extra documents.
channels.requirements: Valid ID for an outward remittance from an FX savings account. Cash remittances above USD 10,000 equivalent per day additionally require the customs-declared inbound form or the original cash-withdrawal slip.
pros: The lightest documentation in the whole system — ID only for account-to-account transfers.
No quota is consumed.
Shows that the hard part is the RMB-to-FX conversion, not the outbound wire.
cons: Does nothing for a CNY balance — you still need a conversion route first.
Banks still run AML monitoring on the wire.

channels.name: Proceeds of selling China property owned by a non-resident
channels.name_zh: 境外个人出售境内商品房所得购汇汇出
channels.applies_to: 境外个人 who sold residential property in China that they owned for own use
channels.best_for: Money that is specifically the net proceeds of a China property sale
channels.cap: No statutory ceiling stated in the rule; the sale must satisfy the self-use principle and the FX rules for the real-estate market.
channels.requirements: SAFE approval (经外汇局核准) before conversion and remittance; purchase must have complied with the self-use principle; supporting documents are those required by the SAFE/Ministry of Construction real-estate FX notice referenced in the implementing rules.
pros: Expressly contemplated by Art. 22 of the individual FX measures.
Uses the property-sale tax clearance that you need anyway to register the transfer.
One of the few capital-account exits written specifically for individuals.
cons: Requires SAFE approval — a discretionary administrative step, not a bank formality.
Only applies to real-estate proceeds; other capital gains have no equivalent individual route.
The property must have been bought for self-use, consistent with the rules on foreigners buying property.
The underlying gain is taxable in China at 20% before any of this can happen.
channels.note: Art. 22 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3; Art. 21 of 汇发[2007]1号 refers to the SAFE/MOC real-estate FX notice. The detail of that notice was not re-verified in this pass — flagged.

channels.name: The USD 50,000 annual facilitation quota
channels.name_zh: 个人年度便利化额度（等值5万美元）
channels.applies_to: 境内个人 for purchases of FX; the annual total for 结汇 applies to all individuals
channels.best_for: Small amounts, or drip-feeding a balance out over many years
channels.cap: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year for 结汇 and for 境内个人购汇 combined with the annual-total framework.
channels.requirements: Valid ID inside the annual total. Above the total, current-account purposes need genuine supporting documents; capital-account purposes follow the capital-account rules.
pros: Simple, branch-level, same-day process with no approval file.
Predictable and repeatable every calendar year.
The most widely understood route, so bank staff handle it routinely.
cons: USD 50,000 a year means 20 years to move USD 1 million — and the rule has not been raised since 2007.
The quota is per person per year and may not be pooled: splitting across family members to evade the limit is expressly prohibited.
It is a current-account facility; using it to fund overseas property or securities is outside what it authorises.
It applies to 境内个人 purchases — a US citizen classified as 境外个人 is not capped by this figure but instead needs source documents.
channels.note: Art. 2 of 汇发[2007]1号; Art. 9 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3.

channels.name: Above-quota current-account purchase with genuine documents
channels.name_zh: 超年度总额经常项目购汇
channels.status_label: Lawful only for a genuine purpose
channels.best_for: Genuine study, medical or travel costs above the annual total
channels.cap: No fixed cap, but bounded by the documented cost of the underlying transaction.
channels.requirements: Valid ID plus documents showing the amount of the transaction (tuition, hospital bills, travel bookings, etc.).
pros: A real way to exceed USD 50,000 for a genuine current-account need.
Documentation is straightforward and verifiable.
cons: Strictly purpose-bound — it cannot be repurposed into a general capital exit.
Presenting a false purpose is illegal arbitrage of FX and is fined on the amount involved.
Each transaction needs its own evidence.
channels.note: Art. 12 of 汇发[2007]1号; Arts. 12 and 40 of the FX Regulations.

channels.name: Resident outbound direct investment (ODI)
channels.name_zh: 境内个人对外直接投资
channels.best_for: Setting up or capitalising a real business abroad
channels.cap: No personal amount cap stated in the individual FX rules; approval and overseas investment FX registration are required.
channels.requirements: SAFE approval to buy FX or use own FX, plus overseas investment FX registration; approval or filing with the competent authorities first where required.
pros: A legitimate capital-account exit, and the only one for genuinely entrepreneurial money.
Once registered, the investment has a documented basis for future profit repatriation.
cons: Not available for moving personal savings — it requires an actual outbound investment project.
Multi-stage approval touching commerce, NDRC and SAFE processes.
Overseas investment also creates US reporting (Forms 5471/8865/926 as applicable) — not covered in this project.
channels.note: Art. 16 of 汇发[2007]1号; Arts. 17 and 22 of the FX Regulations.

channels.name: QDII funds and bank products
channels.name_zh: 合格境内机构投资者（QDII）
channels.best_for: Gaining foreign-currency exposure, not for repatriating cash
channels.requirements: Buy a QDII product through a bank or fund manager that holds the qualification.
pros: Expressly permitted for residents, so no personal approval file.
Converts RMB into foreign-currency assets inside a regulated wrapper.
cons: Your money stays inside the product; redeeming returns RMB to your China account, so it is not an exit.
QDII capacity is rationed and products are sometimes closed to new money.
Adds market risk on top of the currency question.
channels.note: Art. 17 of 汇发[2007]1号. QDII capacity is set institution by institution; no per-person quota figure was confirmed from an official source, so the cap is left blank.

channels.name: Employee stock ownership / share option plans
channels.name_zh: 境外上市公司员工持股计划、认股期权
channels.applies_to: 境内个人 employed by a listed group
channels.best_for: Share-sale proceeds and dividends from your employer's offshore plan
channels.cap: No personal cap stated; approval runs through the employer or domestic agent.
channels.requirements: The employer or domestic agent applies to SAFE for the plan; sale proceeds and dividends are repatriated to a dedicated domestic FX account and may then be converted or moved to your FX savings account.
pros: A genuine, documented route for equity compensation.
Proceeds can lawfully be converted once repatriated.
cons: Only exists if you actually have such a plan and the employer runs the SAFE filing.
The money must come back into China first — it is not a direct offshore exit.
channels.verdict: Not applicable to a bank balance
channels.note: Art. 18 of 汇发[2007]1号.

channels.name: Spending on a Chinese card while abroad
channels.name_zh: 银行卡境外消费
channels.applies_to: Any holder of a mainland-issued card
channels.best_for: Paying real expenses — travel, study, online purchases — without touching FX quotas
channels.cap: Card spending for genuine current-account purposes does not count against the USD 50,000 facilitation quota; the annual RMB 100,000 cap applies to cash withdrawals, not to purchases.
channels.requirements: A mainland-issued card and a genuine underlying purchase.
pros: Spends RMB directly at the point of sale, converting at card-scheme rates.
Does not consume the annual quota.
Needs no approval file of any kind.
cons: You receive goods or services, not dollars — it does not turn a balance into cash you can invest.
Using cards to extract value artificially (fake transactions, refund loops) is a violation, not a workaround.
channels.verdict: Useful for living costs, not for capital
channels.note: SAFE Q&A to 汇发[2017]29号, question 3.

channels.name: Overseas ATM cash withdrawals
channels.name_zh: 银行卡境外提取现金
channels.applies_to: Any holder of a mainland-issued card
channels.best_for: Small, genuine cash needs abroad
channels.cap: RMB 100,000 equivalent per natural person per calendar year across all your cards, and RMB 10,000 equivalent per card per day.
channels.requirements: Your own card. Borrowing or lending cards to get around the cap is prohibited.
pros: A real, published allowance and mechanically easy.
Useful for day-to-day spending money.
cons: RMB 100,000 a year is about USD 14,000 at recent rates — trivial against a large balance.
Exceeding the cap suspends overseas withdrawals for the rest of this year and all of next year, and may be fined.
Cash leaves no paper trail for your US filings and raises CMIR questions above USD 10,000.
Uses the worst FX pricing of any channel (ATM spreads plus fees).
channels.note: 汇发[2017]29号 items 1–2 as described by SAFE.

channels.name: Carrying foreign cash across the border
channels.name_zh: 携带外币现钞出境
channels.status_label: Lawful only up to USD 10,000 after permits
channels.best_for: Almost nothing — this is a theoretical route only
channels.cap: Up to USD 5,000 needs no permit; USD 5,000–10,000 needs a bank-issued 携带证; over USD 10,000 is in principle not allowed and needs a SAFE-issued permit that is reserved for listed special situations.
channels.requirements: Passport, visa, bank deposit proof or purchase documents, and the permit where required; US-side CMIR filing above USD 10,000.
pros: No quota is consumed for amounts within the permit limits.
cons: The ceiling is USD 10,000 — irrelevant to a meaningful balance.
Taking out more without a permit is punishable with a warning and a fine of up to 20% of the amount, on top of customs action.
Physically risky and instantly reportable on the US side above USD 10,000.
Repeated border runs are exactly the pattern enforcement targets.
channels.note: SAFE operations guide citing 汇发[2003]102号; Art. 42 of the FX Regulations; 31 CFR 1010.340 for the US side.

channels.name: Greater Bay Area Wealth Management Connect (跨境理财通)
channels.name_zh: 跨境理财通
channels.applies_to: Mainland residents of the nine GBA mainland cities
channels.best_for: Nothing, unless you are a GBA mainland resident
channels.requirements: GBA mainland household registration (or a qualifying period of local social insurance / income tax), investment experience, and asset or income thresholds; funds run through a closed loop between a remittance account and an investment account.
pros: A genuine cross-border investment channel with a published rulebook.
Closed-loop design means clean documentation.
cons: Requires GBA residency — a US citizen living in the US cannot qualify.
Closed loop: money goes into investments, not into your US bank account.
Individual quota figure left blank and flagged as unverified.
channels.note: Eligibility from the PBOC Guangzhou branch Q&A. An individual investor quota exists but the current figure was not confirmed from an official source, so it is left blank and flagged.

channels.name: Gifting or otherwise transferring property abroad as a resident
channels.name_zh: 境内个人对外捐赠和财产转移
channels.best_for: Nothing in practice — listed here because it is often suggested online
channels.cap: No amount stated; approval is required and discretionary.
channels.requirements: Must comply with the relevant rules and be approved by SAFE.
pros: The only textual basis for an outbound gift, and it exists.
cons: SAFE's own Q&A says any form of individual property transfer other than emigrant or inheritance transfer falls outside the dedicated measures — so there is no ready procedure for a plain gift.
Approval is discretionary and, for a gift of savings, is not a realistic expectation.
Attempting it without approval is an evasion of exchange control, fined on the amount involved.
channels.note: Art. 20 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3; SAFE Q&A Q1; Art. 39 of the FX Regulations.

channels.name: Returning unused inbound FX by the original route
channels.name_zh: 境外个人未使用的境外汇入外汇原路汇回
channels.best_for: Money you wired into China and did not use
channels.cap: No stated amount limit; it must be the same funds, returned the way they came.
channels.requirements: Valid ID; the funds must be identifiable as unused inbound FX.
pros: Very light procedure and no quota consumed.
Statutorily clear.
cons: Only reverses an inbound wire; it cannot create a new outbound flow.
Must still be in FX, not converted into RMB.
channels.note: Art. 14 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3.

channels.name: Crypto or stablecoin conversion
channels.name_zh: 虚拟货币／稳定币兑换
channels.best_for: Nothing
channels.requirements: None — the activity itself is banned.
pros: None that survive contact with the rules. In 2021 this was grey; since 6 February 2026 it is expressly illegal financial activity.
cons: RMB-to-virtual-currency conversion and related services are illegal financial activities that are strictly prohibited and suppressed.
Financial institutions may not open accounts, move funds or settle for such activity, so a bank seeing crypto-linked flows will freeze and report.
Investments contrary to public order are void in civil law and the loss falls on the investor.
US side is no better: the IRS treats virtual currency as property, so every trade is a taxable disposition, and an offshore exchange is an FBAR-reportable account.
channels.note: 银发〔2026〕42号, section 1(1) and section 6(19), which replaced 银发〔2021〕237号.

channels.name: Underground banks / offsetting pairs (地下钱庄、对敲)
channels.name_zh: 地下钱庄、对敲
channels.best_for: Nothing
channels.requirements: None — the activity is a crime.
pros: Speed and apparent convenience are the only selling points, and both are illusory.
cons: Private or disguised FX trading carries a warning, confiscation of the proceeds and a fine of up to 30% of the amount, rising to 30%–100% where serious.

Where the amount reaches RMB 5,000,000 of turnover or RMB 100,000 of gains, it is prosecuted as illegal business operation under Art. 225(4) of the Criminal Law; RMB 25,000,000 or RMB 500,000 of gains is 'especially serious'.
If money laundering is also made out, the heavier charge applies.
Counterparties routinely abscond or freeze funds, and there is no legal recourse because the contract is unlawful.
US exposure: an unreported offshore account used for this is a willful FBAR fact pattern, where the penalty reaches 50% of the balance.
channels.note: Arts. 45 and 39 of the FX Regulations; 法释〔2019〕1号 Arts. 2–5.

channels.name: Smurfing / 'ants moving house' (蚂蚁搬家) — pooling relatives' quotas
channels.name_zh: 蚂蚁搬家、分拆购汇
channels.best_for: Nothing
channels.requirements: None — splitting to evade limits is prohibited.
pros: It is the most commonly recommended workaround online, which is exactly why it is watched.
cons: The individual FX measures directly prohibit using splitting (分拆) to evade limit supervision, and prohibit false commercial documents.
Each participant's quota is personal; pooling is evasion of exchange control, fined on the amount involved up to 30% (30%–100% if serious).
Banks' FX systems record every conversion against the individual, so the pattern is visible in aggregate.
It creates a paper trail that both tax authorities can reconstruct, including the relatives' own tax positions.
channels.note: Art. 7 of PBC Order [2006] No. 3; Arts. 39–40 of the FX Regulations; SAFE's card Q&A repeats the no-borrowing rule.

channels.name: False trade or service documents
channels.name_zh: 虚假贸易单证、虚构服务贸易
channels.best_for: Nothing
channels.requirements: None — the activity is illegal.
pros: None.
cons: Using false or invalid transaction documents to buy FX is illegal arbitrage, punished by forced re-conversion and a fine of up to 30% of the amount (30%–100% if serious).
Fabricating payments to obtain settlement is separately criminal as illegal business operation.
The invoicing party is exposed to VAT and invoice offences in China as well as FX penalties.
Once the money is abroad, the US tax return still has to explain the source or it becomes unreported income.
channels.note: Arts. 40 and 48 of the FX Regulations; 法释〔2019〕1号 Art. 1.

channels.name: Hold the RMB and do nothing
channels.name_zh: 继续持有人民币
channels.best_for: Buying time while you assemble documents, or if the balance is small
channels.requirements: None.
pros: Zero transaction cost and zero penalty exposure.
The account remains FBAR/8938-reportable, but reporting is cheap compared with penalties for not reporting.
Useful while you gather the household-registration and tax documents the approved routes need.
cons: You keep full CNY/USD currency risk on the whole balance.
China has no deposit insurance comparable to the US and account access can be restricted for identity reasons.
It does not stop the clock on US reporting obligations.
channels.note: Included as the benchmark every other channel is measured against.
